RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Escape of Water and Ancillary Plant Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods, percentages and optional extensions shown in square
brackets or marked as optional are those stated in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered, and which of the optional extensions
apply, is agreed between insurer and policyholder and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies the cost
of putting it back, on an index-linked reinstatement basis with an enhancement.
A range of consequential expenses triggered by a loss event is also carried,
within the limits agreed for each head.

Two distinctions run through the whole of this wording. The first is between the
escape that causes a loss and the damage that escape causes: damage to insured
property is indemnified even where the installation from which the water escaped
is not itself insured property, while putting that installation back into working
order is a separate matter governed by 2.4.4, 4.4.2 and 7.1.8. The second is
between the parts and items the loss actually reached and those it did not: the
first are made good, the second are not, however sensible it may be to treat them
at the same time.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.

Affected part or item - a room, surface, building component, finish, fitting,
installation or furnishing on which physical damage caused by the insured event
is established by the loss investigation - by inspection, by photographic record,
by technical measurement or by a technical report - taken at or shortly after the
time of the loss. An item on which no such damage is established is not an
affected item, whatever its proximity to the affected ones and whatever the risk
that it might have been reached.

Source installation - the pipe, vessel, plant or equipment from which the water
escaped, whether or not it is insured property.

Repair cost - the outlay directed at making good the physical damage caused by
the insured event on an affected part or item. Outlay that pursues any other
purpose is not a repair cost, however it may be described or invoiced.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the itemised labour and materials:
call-out and travel, carriage, delivery, disposal, administration, handling and
comparable items.

Optional extension - a widening of the cover which applies only where it is
recorded in the schedule. Where an extension is not recorded, the base wording
applies unchanged.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.

Secured lenders - creditors whose claim is secured by a charge registered against
the property. The interests of secured lenders enjoy statutory protection.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or lost
as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1).

2.3 The fire group defined

2.3.1 Fire is a combustion that has started without a hearth intended for it, or
that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of spreading under its own
power. Lightning strike is the direct passage of a lightning discharge onto
property. Overvoltage caused by lightning covers damage through overvoltage,
overcurrent or short circuit in insured electrical installations and appliances.

2.3.2 Explosion and deflagration are suddenly running force events resting on the
tendency of gases or vapours to expand; implosion is a sudden collapse of a
hollow body under external overpressure.

2.3.3 The impact or crash of an aircraft, its parts or its cargo is covered, as
is the impact of a road, rail or water-borne vehicle, save where its keeper or
driver is the policyholder or an occupant of the building.

2.3.4 Scorch damage arising out of one of the events above is covered; scorch
damage from any other cause up to [amount]. Smoke and soot damage arising out of
one of those events is covered; damage from the gradual action of smoke or soot
is not.

2.3.5 Not covered within this group is damage caused by earthquake; damage to
internal combustion engines from explosions inside the combustion chamber; and
damage at the switching elements of electrical switches from the gas pressure
inside them, unless the consequence of an insured fire event.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.1 The three headings
The escape of water peril covers three things: damage caused by escaping water;
fracture damage to insured pipework inside buildings; and fracture damage to
insured pipework outside buildings.

2.4.2 Damage caused by escaping water
Escaping water means water that has emerged, contrary to its intended purpose,
from a water-carrying installation situated on the insured site. It is immaterial
for this heading whether the source installation is itself insured property,
whether it belongs to the building or to a separate facility on the site, and
whether the water it carried was drawn from the mains supply or held in a basin,
tank or circuit.

Covered under this heading is the damage the escaping water causes to insured
property: the wetting, soaking, staining, swelling, distortion, detachment,
corrosion, contamination and comparable physical impairment of the affected
rooms, surfaces, components, finishes, fittings, installations and furnishings,
together with the consequential damage arising from it. The path the water took
determines the extent of the cover: rooms into which the water ran, and the parts
and items within them that it reached, are covered wherever they lie on that
path, including ancillary and plant rooms.

Operating fluids from heating, air-conditioning, circulation and treatment
systems, and steam, also count as escaping water. Fluids intended for the
generation of energy do not.

2.4.3 Fracture damage to insured pipework
Covered inside buildings is frost-related and other fracture damage to the pipes
of the water and gas supply, of heating and air-conditioning systems, of
water-based extinguishing and sprinkler systems and of rainwater drainage,
together with frost-related fracture damage to the sanitary fittings, valves,
radiators, boilers and comparable parts of those systems. Covered outside
buildings is frost-related and other fracture damage to supply pipes of the water
supply and to pipes of heating or air-conditioning systems, insofar as the
policyholder bears the risk for them and insofar as they serve the supply of
insured buildings or are situated on the insured site.

This heading presupposes in every case that the pipework concerned is insured
property under Part 4.

2.4.4 The source installation
Putting the source installation back into working order is not part of the
indemnity under 2.4.2.

Where the source installation is insured property - because it falls within 2.4.3
or because an optional extension under 4.4.2 applies to it - its repair is
indemnified under 2.4.3, together with the labour, components, fittings,
connections and sealing materials belonging to that repair.

Where the source installation is not insured property, neither its repair nor the
skilled or unskilled labour, the components, fittings, connections, sealing,
refilling, recommissioning or functional testing belonging to that repair is
indemnified, however plainly its failure caused the covered damage, on whichever
invoice those items appear, and by whichever trade they are billed.

Locating the escape, and establishing where the water went and what it wetted,
falls under 5.2.2 in either case and is not affected by the status of the source
installation.

2.4.5 Exclusions within this peril
Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where named: splash or cleaning water; dry rot and house-rot fungi
of every kind; groundwater, standing or flowing surface water, flood,
precipitation, or a backing-up brought about by any of these; earthquake, snow
load, avalanche, volcanic eruption; ground subsidence or landslip, unless
escaping water within the meaning of 2.4.2 caused it; the perils of the fire
group; the opening of sprinklers on account of fire, pressure testing or works;
storm or hail. Damage to buildings or parts of buildings that are not ready for
occupation is not covered.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

2.5.1 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength; hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice. Only damage arising from the direct
action of storm or hail on insured property, on buildings in which insured
property is located, or on buildings structurally joined to them, is covered,
together with damage caused by objects thrown onto them.

2.5.2 The further natural hazards are flood, backing-up of water, earthquake,
ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as
customarily defined.

2.5.3 Not covered is damage caused by storm surge; by the penetration of
precipitation or dirt through openings that were not properly closed; by
groundwater save where it emerged at the surface as a result of precipitation or
overflow; by the perils of the fire group, save where triggered by an insured
earthquake; and by drought or desiccation.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract.

3.1.5 Upkeep, servicing and inspection of installations
Outlay directed at the servicing, maintenance, cleaning, adjustment, periodic
testing, certification or general condition of an installation is not
indemnifiable. This applies irrespective of whether the measure was performed on
the occasion of an insured event, was recommended in its aftermath, or was
carried out by a trade that also performed covered work.

This clause does not affect the measures described in 7.1.7, which are directed
at parts and items the loss actually reached and at their return to service.
Where an installation that is insured property was itself reached by the escaping
water, the examination, cleaning, flushing, drying, making good and
recommissioning of that installation necessitated by the ingress are treated as
making good under 7.1.7 and not as upkeep under this clause.

3.1.6 Precautionary and preventive measures
Renewing, replacing or upgrading a part or item on which no damage from the
insured event has been established is not indemnifiable, even where the measure
is taken as a precaution, on a technical recommendation, because the part or item
stands next to or in the same room as an affected one, or because a later failure
is thought possible. Establishing whether such a part or item was reached falls
under 5.2.2 and 7.1.7(g); replacing it where it was not falls under this clause.

3.2 Exclusions within the fire group

See 2.3.5.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

See 2.4.4 and 2.4.5.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

See 2.5.3.

3.5 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts and items of the insured property that were
themselves affected by the insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not
constitute a repair cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is
governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the buildings identified in the schedule, their
building components, their building accessories, terraces on the insured site
that directly adjoin the building, further site installations named in the
schedule, and the optional extensions recorded there.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground, capable of affording protection
against external influences and intended for predominantly residential use.
Conservatories, garden rooms, enclosed pool halls, plant and machinery rooms and
comparable rooms count as part of the building insofar as they are structurally
connected to it and enclosed.

4.2.2 Building components
Items incorporated into a building that have lost their independence through
their firm connection with it, together with the fitting-out elements of the
dwelling: floor coverings with their bedding, adhesive, underlay, insulating and
levelling layers; wall and ceiling finishes; interior doors; and fixed trim,
skirting, beading and comparable edging elements.

4.2.3 Building accessories and furnishings
Movable items located inside the building which serve the upkeep of the insured
building or its predominant intended purpose, together with the loose furnishings
of the affected rooms insofar as this is agreed in the schedule. Recreational,
decorative, horticultural and comparable loose articles - among them the
equipment, floats, covers and toys belonging to a water feature, and planters,
pots, plants and their contents - are not building accessories and are not
insured property.

4.2.4 Building services installations
The electrical, water, heating, air-conditioning, ventilation and comparable
technical installations serving the building are insured property insofar as they
serve the building itself and are not excluded under 4.3.

4.2.5 Terraces and further site installations
Terraces are paved surfaces intended for occupation in the open air. Further site
installations are the items firmly connected with the ground and soil of the
insured site listed in the schedule.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components, including a permanently
      connected electricity storage installation;
  (b) swimming pools, plunge pools, whirlpools, basins, ponds and comparable
      water features, whether sunk, raised, indoor or outdoor, together with
      their shells, linings, covers, surrounds and steps, and together with the
      whole of their technical plant - the supply, circulation, return, overflow
      and drainage pipework, the connections, valves and fittings, the pumps,
      filters, heat exchangers, dosing and treatment equipment, and the control
      and monitoring systems belonging to them - whether located inside or
      outside the building and whether or not connected to an insured
      installation. This exclusion does not apply where the optional extension
      under 4.4.2 is recorded in the schedule;
  (c) items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner at that person's own expense and at that person's own
      risk, unless co-insured under 4.4.1;
  (d) electronically stored data and programs;
  (e) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace an
      affected item of the same kind and intended purpose.

The exclusion of an installation under this clause does not exclude the damage
that an escape from it causes to insured property (2.4.2). It excludes the
installation itself, its repair, its replacement, its refilling and
recommissioning, and every measure directed at it as such.

4.4 Optional extensions

4.4.1 Items subsequently incorporated by a tenant or condominium owner, and the
loose furnishings of the insured rooms, can be co-insured where this is agreed.

4.4.2 Water features and their technical plant
By way of departure from 4.3(b), a water feature situated on the insured site
together with the whole of its technical plant can be co-insured where this is
recorded in the schedule. Where that extension applies:
  (a) the feature and its plant are insured property for all purposes of these
      conditions;
  (b) fracture and comparable failure of its pipework, connections and fittings
      falls under 2.4.3, so that its repair, the labour hours spent on that
      repair and the materials consumed by it are indemnified under 2.4.4;
  (c) the examination of the plant, and the cleaning, flushing, servicing and
      recommissioning of it necessitated by the escape or by the ingress of
      water, count as making good under 7.1.7 and not as upkeep under 3.1.5.

Where the extension is not recorded in the schedule, 4.3(b), 2.4.4 and 3.1.5
apply unchanged, and every measure directed at the feature or its plant - its
repair, the labour and materials belonging to that repair, its examination and
its servicing - is outside the cover, even where the plant stands in an affected
room.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel or parcels on which the
insured building stands.

4.6 Condominium and part-ownership units

Where the contract is with an association of condominium owners and the insurer
is wholly or partly released from liability on account of the conduct of
individual owners, it remains obliged to pay the remaining owners in respect of
their separate property and their shares in the common property. The remaining
owners may claim indemnity for the co-ownership share concerned where the
additional indemnity is applied to reinstating the common property; the owner
concerned must reimburse the insurer. These provisions apply correspondingly to
part-ownership units.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set out
in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the covered
settlement, irrespective of the number of trades or invoices involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) emergency and mitigation measures, including the extraction, pumping and
      removal of escaped water and the securing of the affected rooms;
  (b) locating the escape and establishing the extent of the wetting;
  (c) debris removal and disposal costs;
  (d) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (e) costs of lost water, gas and heating oil, and of electricity lost from
      storage installations;
  (f) hotel costs;
  (g) costs of returning early from a holiday.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Emergency and mitigation measures
Costs of the measures taken during or immediately after the insured event to end
the escape, to remove the water that has escaped and to prevent the damage from
increasing, capped at [amount] per insured event. Shutting off, isolating or
temporarily closing the source installation counts as such a measure; repairing
it is governed by 2.4.4.

5.2.2 Locating the escape and establishing the extent of the wetting
Costs of the technical measures needed to find where the water emerged and to
determine which rooms, surfaces, components and installations it reached and how
far they are wetted - moisture measurement, surveying, mapping, technical
reporting and comparable investigation - together with the follow-up measurements
needed to establish that the drying is complete. These costs are reimbursed
whether or not the source installation is insured property, whether the search
runs from the room where the damage showed to the room where the escape began,
and whether they are billed by the trade that carries out the drying or by
another.

5.2.3 Debris removal and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away, removing and disposing of the material taken out
in the course of the covered works, including transport to the nearest disposal
site and the disposal charge itself. This head is reimbursed once per insured
event for the material concerned; a further charge for the same removal on the
invoice of another trade falls under 7.1.8(f).

5.2.4 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting property, where those measures
serve to reinstate or replace insured property.

5.2.5 Lost water, gas, heating oil and stored electricity
Costs arising because these escaped or were lost contrary to their intended
purpose as a result of an insured event, capped at [amount] per insured event.
The cost of refilling an installation excluded under 4.3 does not fall under this
head.

5.2.6 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation where the dwelling permanently occupied by the
policyholder has become uninhabitable and confining themselves to a habitable
part of it cannot reasonably be expected, reimbursed only to the extent that they
exceed the indemnity payable for rental value and only where indemnity cannot be
claimed under another insurance contract, up to [amount] per day for a maximum of
[number] days.

5.2.7 Early return from holiday
Additional travel costs arising because the policyholder, or a person living with
them in the same household, breaks off a holiday trip prematurely on account of a
significant insured event, in a reasonable amount and capped at [amount] per
insured event.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent or terminated the tenancy on account of an insured
event, and the locally customary rental value of residential premises occupied by
the policyholder itself where use cannot reasonably be expected, in each case
including the running service charges in the sense of tenancy law.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.

5.5 Commercially used premises

For commercially used premises, insurance of loss of rent or of the locally
customary rental value can be agreed.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. The insurable
value determined for the building applies equally to building components,
building accessories, terraces and further site installations.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

6.2.1 What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the buildings
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event. Architects'
fees and other construction and planning costs form part of that value.

6.2.2 Two elements are built into that value: additional costs arising from
public-law restrictions on reinstatement, and price increases arising between the
occurrence of the insured event and reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.2.3 The insurer tracks the cover against the development of building costs.

6.2.4 The basis of cover determines the standard to which the affected parts and
items are put back. It does not extend the indemnity to parts, items or
installations that are outside the cover under Part 4, it does not extend it to
parts and items the loss did not reach, and it does not fund a standard above the
one in place before the loss (7.1.9).

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted or
    delayed

For buildings that are not reinstated, or are reinstated late, only the
index-linked current value with enhancement is insured - the enhanced new-build
value at the time of the insured event, less depreciation for age and wear.

6.4 Market value for permanently devalued buildings

For buildings designated for demolition, or otherwise permanently devalued, only
the achievable sale price excluding the land share is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and fit-out, the use, the optional extensions recorded in the
schedule, other agreed features material to the premium calculation, and the
adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of a
construction price index for residential buildings and a collectively agreed wage
index for the construction sector, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings - the locally customary reinstatement costs at the
      time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings and other damaged property - the necessary repair
      costs at the time of the insured event, together with any diminution in
      value the repair does not offset, capped at the insurable value;
  (c) for destroyed or lost other property - the replacement price for property
      of the same kind and quality in new condition at the time of the insured
      event.

7.1.2 Where technically still usable substance may not be used for reinstatement
because of public-law requirements, the policyholder receives corresponding
indemnity, provided the orders in question were not already in force before the
insured event.

7.1.3 Price increases occurring between the insured event and reinstatement are
indemnified where reinstatement is secured within three years.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts and items of the insured property that were
themselves affected by the insured event, as established by the loss
investigation. Work carried out on a room, surface, component, item or
installation that was not itself affected is not covered, even where it is
carried out so that treated and untreated parts correspond in appearance; for
reasons of convenience or economy; as a precaution against a future failure
(3.1.6); at the same time as covered work or in the course of it; or by the same
contractor as the covered work and invoiced together with it.

Where an affected room was wetted as a whole, the whole of that room is treated
as affected for the purposes of extraction, drying and the reinstatement of its
finishes. A separate room that the water did not enter is not brought into the
cover by adjoining an affected one.

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only where a corresponding
replacement material is no longer obtainable and a visible discontinuity would
otherwise remain.

7.1.7 Preparatory, drying and ancillary work forming part of the repair
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) include:
  (a) taking down, dismantling and disposing of the affected components and
      finishes;
  (b) the extraction and removal of standing water, and the drying,
      dehumidification and moisture-removal of the affected rooms, surfaces,
      cavities and components - including the provision, delivery, setting up,
      running, monitoring and collection of the drying, dehumidification and air
      circulation equipment used, and the skilled labour attending it - for as
      long as the measurements under 5.2.2 show the drying to be incomplete;
  (c) the preparation of the substrate or supporting structure before a new
      finish is applied;
  (d) materials of a type, quality, grade and specification corresponding to
      those in place immediately before the insured event, including any bedding,
      adhesive, sealing, underlay, insulating or levelling layer that formed part
      of the component as installed before the loss;
  (e) unaffected trim, skirting, beading, edging and comparable finishing
      elements that have to be taken off in order to repair an affected component
      and that cannot be refitted afterwards;
  (f) the cleaning, drying and where necessary the replacement of affected
      furnishings insofar as they are insured property;
  (g) the examination and testing of an installation that was itself reached by
      the escaping water, insofar as that examination is necessary to establish
      whether the installation may safely be returned to service or must be made
      good, together with the making good, replacement and recommissioning it
      shows to be necessary. This applies to installations that are insured
      property, including those brought into the cover by an extension under
      4.4.2. Where the examination establishes that a component was not reached,
      its renewal falls under 3.1.6; where a technical report establishes that a
      component was reached, its renewal falls under this heading;
  (h) the final cleaning of the working area on completion of the covered works,
      including the removal of the residues and dust generated by those works.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however
they may be described, bundled or invoiced, by whichever trade they are raised,
and irrespective of whether they appear on an invoice that also contains covered
work:

  (a) the repair, replacement, sealing, reconnection, refilling, recommissioning
      or functional testing of the source installation where that installation is
      not insured property (2.4.4), together with the skilled and unskilled
      labour hours, the components, fittings and consumable materials
      attributable to that work, whether billed as one line or as several, and
      whether billed by the trade that located the escape or by another;

  (b) measures directed at the servicing, maintenance, cleaning, adjustment,
      periodic testing, certification, general condition, tidiness, upkeep,
      modernisation or improvement of an installation or of the insured property,
      as distinct from making good the damage caused by the insured event
      (3.1.5). This includes every measure directed at an installation that is
      not insured property, even where that installation stands in an affected
      room, and the examination or testing of an installation that the escaping
      water did not reach;

  (c) the renewal or replacement of a part or item on which no damage from the
      insured event has been established (3.1.6);

  (d) the improvement element where a replacement of a higher grade, superior
      material, larger format or premium range is chosen. Where the affected
      status of the component and its specification immediately before the loss
      are established under 7.1.10, indemnity for that work is the cost of the
      standard-grade equivalent corresponding to what was in place before the
      loss and the difference is borne by the policyholder; where they are not
      established, so that the outlay is shown only as an improvement and not as
      the making good of an affected component, no part of it is indemnified;

  (e) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to
      the repair - its own tools and consumable small equipment, its own
      diagnostic and measuring devices as such, provisioning, catering,
      refreshment and comparable subsistence for its own personnel, and general
      administrative, handling, order-processing or documentation charges levied
      in addition to itemised labour and materials;

  (f) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades;
      only the first such charge is indemnified. This applies in particular to a
      removal, disposal or drying charge raised again on the invoice of a second
      trade for material or equipment already accounted for on the invoice of the
      first;

  (g) call-out, travel, journey, mileage, vehicle, attendance and standby
      charges, save where incurred on the occasion of, and on the same invoice
      as, work that is itself indemnifiable; where nothing billed on an invoice
      is indemnifiable, the attendance charge on that invoice is not
      indemnifiable either. Where indemnifiable, one such charge per invoice is
      reimbursed; second attendances, return visits and repeat journeys in
      respect of the same insured event are not.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, format, material
and specification in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher
specification, a larger format, a superior material or a premium range is chosen
instead, 7.1.8(d) governs. Where the pre-existing material is no longer
obtainable, the nearest currently available equivalent of the same grade sets the
ceiling; an unavoidable difference is not treated as an improvement, a chosen one
is.

7.1.10 Evidence and apportionment
The policyholder demonstrates, for each item and each head of cost claimed, the
affected part or item to which it relates, the physical damage established on it,
its type and specification immediately before the loss where a replacement is
claimed, and the making-good purpose the outlay serves.

Where an invoice line bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable elements and
the elements can be identified and valued from the documents, the line is
apportioned and the indemnifiable elements are paid. Where they cannot be
separated, the line is assessed by its predominant stated purpose; where the
predominant purpose is not indemnifiable, the line is not indemnified. Labour
hours billed without an indication of the work performed are allocated to the
non-indemnifiable element where the invoice on which they appear is predominantly
directed at the source installation.

7.2 Market value

Insofar as a building is designated for demolition or otherwise permanently
devalued, insured property is indemnified at the achievable sale price excluding
the land share.

7.3 Construction specification lower or higher than described

Where the actual construction specification at the time of the insured event is
of lower value than described in the contract, the insurer is not obliged to
compensate more than the loss actually incurred. Where it is of higher value, the
indemnity is based on the specification described in the contract.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred, and the indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.5 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses the insured loss of rent or rental value up to the end of
the agreed period.

7.6 The reinstatement element of the indemnity

The policyholder acquires a claim to that part of the indemnity which exceeds the
current-value loss only where it ensures that the indemnity will be used to
reinstate or replace insured property of the same kind and intended purpose at
the previous location, and where reinstatement or replacement is secured within
three years of the occurrence of the insured event.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the reinstatement or replacement, and not where the
policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed, once per
insured event.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum. That part of the indemnity which goes beyond the
current-value loss falls due once the policyholder has demonstrated that it has
secured the reinstatement or replacement.

7.10 Repayment of the reinstatement element

The policyholder must repay indemnity paid on the reinstatement basis where,
through its own fault, the property was not reinstated or replaced within a
reasonable period.

7.11 Interest

The indemnity bears interest from the notification of the loss, save where paid
within one month. The rate is [number] percentage point(s) below the applicable
statutory base rate, but at least [percentage] and at most [percentage] per year.

7.12 Suspension of time limits

Any period during which the indemnity cannot be determined or paid owing to the
fault of the policyholder is left out of account.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are pending, or a legally required involvement
of a secured lender has not taken place.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the
amount of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer
and policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly, and may agree to
extend it to further determinations relating to the insured event.

8.2 Each party nominates one expert in text form. Where a party fails to nominate
within two weeks of a request, the requesting party may have the expert appointed
by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location. Before beginning
their determinations, the two experts nominate a third expert as umpire.

8.3 The experts' findings must state a schedule of the affected insured property
with the corresponding insurable values; the reinstatement and repair costs; the
residual values; and the insured costs and insured loss of rent or rental value.
Where the source installation is not insured property, the findings state the
outlay attributable to it separately from the outlay attributable to the affected
insured property. Where a measure was carried out on a part or item whose
affected status is disputed, the findings state on what evidence that status
rests.

8.4 Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the
findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute within the
limits set by the experts' findings. The findings are binding unless they
manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of affairs.

8.5 Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert; the costs of the umpire are borne in equal shares.

8.6 The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Contractually agreed safety requirements before an insured event

9.1.1 Insured property must be kept in proper condition at all times. This applies
in particular to water-carrying installations and equipment, to roofs and to items
attached to the exterior. Defects or damage must be remedied without delay.

9.1.2 Water-carrying installations situated on the insured site which are not
insured property must likewise be kept in proper condition, inspected and serviced
in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, and shut off and drained when
out of use for a prolonged period. The cost of doing so is borne by the
policyholder (3.1.5), unless an extension under 4.4.2 applies, in which case 3.1.5
continues to govern routine servicing while making good after an ingress falls
under 7.1.7.

9.1.3 Buildings or parts of buildings that are not in use must be inspected
sufficiently frequently at every time of year, and their water-carrying
installations shut off, drained and kept drained.

9.1.4 During the cold season all buildings and parts of buildings must be heated
and checked sufficiently frequently, or their water-carrying installations shut
off, drained and kept drained.

9.1.5 Backflow prevention devices must be kept operational and the drainage lines
on the insured site kept clear.

9.2 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of these duties, and subject to the conditions
set out in the general contract provisions, the insurer is entitled to terminate
the contract and may be wholly or partly released from liability.

9.3 Circumstances constituting an increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where a
circumstance changes about which the insurer asked before the contract was
concluded; where the building or the predominant part of it is no longer in use;
where construction work removes the roof or renders the building predominantly
unusable; where a water feature or comparable installation is added to the insured
site or to the building, or its plant is materially altered; where a commercial
operation is taken up or changed within the building; or where the building is
placed under heritage protection after conclusion of the contract.

9.4 Consequences of an increase in risk

The consequences of an increase in risk are governed by the general contract
provisions.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION, SECURED LENDERS, TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation where a security right has been registered

Where a secured lender has registered its charge over the property, cancellation
by the policyholder in respect of the fire peril group is effective only where the
policyholder demonstrated, at least one month before expiry of the insurance
contract, either that the property was no longer encumbered with the charge at the
point at which cancellation was at the latest permissible, or that the secured
lender consented to the cancellation. This does not apply to a cancellation
following a disposal of the property or in the insured event.

10.2 Legal position following a transfer of ownership

Where the policyholder disposes of the insured property, the acquirer steps into
its place in the insurance contract at the time of the transfer of ownership; in
the case of real property, at the date of registration in the land register.
Seller and acquirer are jointly and severally liable for the premium for the
insurance period in which the transfer occurs. The insurer need only recognise the
acquirer's entry once it becomes aware of it.

10.3 Rights of cancellation on a transfer of ownership

The insurer may cancel as against the acquirer observing a notice period of one
month; that right lapses if not exercised within one month of the insurer becoming
aware of the disposal. The acquirer may cancel with immediate effect or with
effect from the end of the current insurance period, in text form; that right
lapses one month after acquisition, or one month after the acquirer becomes aware
that the insurance exists. On such a cancellation the seller alone remains liable
for the premium.

10.4 Duties of notification

The disposal must be notified to the insurer without delay in text form by the
seller or the acquirer. Where notification has been omitted, the insurer is not
obliged to pay in the insured event where the event occurred later than one month
after notification ought to have been received and the insurer demonstrates that
it would not have concluded the existing contract with the acquirer. The insurer
remains obliged to pay where it was aware of the disposal, or where the period for
its cancellation had already expired without cancellation at the time of the
insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 11 - LOSS DESCRIPTION AND OPERATIVE PROVISIONS FOR THIS CLAIM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

11.1 Water escaped, contrary to its intended purpose, from a water-carrying
installation situated on the insured site and serving a water feature. The escape
ran through an enclosed room forming part of the insured building and onwards into
an adjoining ancillary and plant room, wetting the floor and wall finishes, the
edging elements, a furnishing item and part of the building's own technical
installations along that path. Rooms and outbuildings which the water did not
enter, and loose recreational and horticultural articles, were not affected within
the meaning of these conditions.

11.2 Whether the feature and its plant are insured property in this claim depends
on whether the extension under 4.4.2 is recorded in the schedule. Where it is,
2.4.3, 2.4.4 and 4.4.2(b) and (c) govern the repair of the failed connection, the
labour hours and materials belonging to it, and the examination and servicing of
the plant. Where it is not, 4.3(b), 2.4.4 and 3.1.5 place all of that outside the
cover, while leaving the damage the escape caused to insured property fully within
it.

11.3 Invoices were rendered by one or more trades. They combine the location of
the escape and the measurement of the wetting; the removal of the standing water,
the drying of the affected rooms and the equipment used for it; the renewal of
affected finishes and edging elements and the making good of affected wall
surfaces; the treatment of an affected furnishing item; the examination of the
building installations on the water's path and the renewal of components within
them; work directed at the water feature and its plant; a replacement of a floor
covering in a material of higher grade than the one in place before the loss;
removal and disposal charges; provisioning for site personnel; final cleaning; and
attendance charges including a repeat attendance.

11.4 The indemnity is determined by separating, line by line, the outlay directed
at parts and items the water reached from the outlay directed at parts and items
it did not, at the source installation where that is not insured property, and at
matters of upkeep; by apportioning bundled lines under 7.1.10 where their elements
can be identified; by applying 7.1.8(d) and 7.1.9 to the choice of specification;
and by reimbursing one attendance charge on each invoice that contains
indemnifiable work.

11.5 Clauses 2.4.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.4, 3.1.5, 3.1.6, 4.2.3, 4.3(b), 4.4.2, 5.2.1,
5.2.2, 5.2.3, 6.2.4, 7.1.1, 7.1.5, 7.1.7(b), 7.1.7(f), 7.1.7(g), 7.1.7(h),
7.1.8(a) to (g), 7.1.9, 7.1.10 and 7.8 are the operative provisions for
determining how each line of each invoice in this claim is characterised.

case.description:
The pool house claim at the big villa. A connection on the indoor pool's supply pipe separated while the owners were away and ran for hours, and the water spread from the pool room into the conservatory and down into the plant room below.

The usual consequential mess followed - a soaked rug in the conservatory seating area, wet wall surfaces in the plant room, and worry about the electrical components stored down there. The pool's own supply pipework needed repairing at the separated connection, and the pool filtration got a going-over as well.

The point to note on this one is the cover. Checking the file, this policyholder does hold the separate Pool Equipment Endorsement and it is attached to the policy, so the pool technology side of the work is not sitting outside cover the way it would on a bare Water Damage section. The owner did still choose to upgrade the floor to a high-end natural stone while the work was open.
